results.title: Supabase Pricing Page and Costs Explained (2026)
results.content:
### Database Size

Supabase's Free tier comes with a 500 MB database size per project. If you want a larger disk size, you'll need to upgrade to paid plans.

Each project on the Pro and Team plans includes an 8 GB disk size. Once you exceed this limit, you pay $0.125 per GB per month.

The cost grows as your product stores more user data, logs, or analytics. Most production applications can quickly hit this limit as usage increases.

### Bandwidth (Egress) [...] ### Free Tier

Supabase's Free plan is built for hobby projects, learning, and basic website development.

Image

Source: Supabase.com

You can use a Postgres database and access community support without any upfront cost. You also get unlimited API requests.

However, Free tier limits apply.

There’s a cap of 50,000 monthly active users, a 500 MB database size, 5 GB egress, and 1 GB file storage. [...] Supabase is not costly for small teams or early-stage startups. The Free tier offers generous limits, while the Pro plan starts at $25/month. Costs only increase when your app uses more compute, storage, bandwidth, monthly active users, or paid add-ons.

### Is Supabase cheaper than AWS?

Supabase can be cheaper and easier to budget than AWS because it offers predictable pricing plans. AWS may provide more services, but pricing can be harder to predict across multiple products.

results.title: Can a Supabase Postgres database scale as my app grows? | Supabase Knowledge Base
results.content:
For database size and disk space, these are included with your plan and range from 500MB database size on the Free plan to fully customized database and disk size for Enterprise plans. Projects on the Pro plan and higher additionally have autoscaling disks.

You can also scale compute as needed. Free projects run on Nano compute and new paid projects start on Micro, and you can move to larger sizes as you need more CPU, memory, and connections. For details refer to Compute pricing.
